name: immunoglobulin heavy locus

function.text: IGH is the immunoglobulin heavy-chain locus; its variable, diversity, joining, and constant segments support antibody production through somatic rearrangement in B cells.

function.text: IGH is the immunoglobulin heavy-chain locus, containing variable, diversity, joining, and constant segments. During B-cell development, DNA rearrangement assembles a variable region by joining diversity and joining segments and then a variable segment. Subsequent class switching changes the constant-region context. Segment recombination, junctional diversity, and somatic hypermutation contribute to the range of antigen recognition without each antibody specificity corresponding to a separate inherited gene.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving IGH have been reported in plasmacytoma, Burkitt lymphoma, and follicular lymphoma.
